record.original_question: Does every metric on a compact surface of positive genus have a geodesic that is dense in the surface?

evidence.quote: Does every metric on a compact surface of positive genus have a geodesic that is dense in the surface?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth closed (compact, without boundary) orientable surface of genus $g \geq 1$, and let $\rho$ be any smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$. A geodesic $\gamma:\mathbb{R}\to\Sigma$ of $(\Sigma,\rho)$ is called dense if its image $\gamma(\mathbb{R})$ is a dense subset of $\Sigma$. Determine whether, for every choice of $\Sigma$ of positive genus and every smooth Riemannian metric $\rho$ on $\Sigma$, there exists at least one dense geodesic on $(\Sigma,\rho)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears as an open problem in the Burns–Matveev list of open problems and questions about geodesics (American Institute of Mathematics). No resolution is indicated in subsequent literature found via search.
